About the survey

Who is putting what in our public space

Our Space is a working model of how much of a walk through New York is watched, and by whom. It gathers the cameras and sensors entering the public realm — fixed CCTV, license-plate readers, bus-lane and red-light enforcement cameras, rideshare dashcams, and the speculative near future of smart glasses and sidewalk delivery robots — onto a single map, then estimates how many of them could capture you as you move. It is an honest estimate, not a surveillance feed: every count carries a confidence tier, and nothing here claims that a specific device saw a specific person.

The fixed-camera layer is built from Amnesty International's crowdsourced Decode Surveillance NYC census and Dahir et al. (2025) machine-vision detections — aggregated, de-duplicated across sources, and recall-corrected. Plate readers come from DeFlock via OpenStreetMap; traffic and enforcement cameras from NYC DOT (locations only — no imagery is used). The moving cameras are modeled, not tracked: rideshare-dashcam density from NYC TLC trip records, and ACE bus routes from MTA GTFS.

Exposure along a route is computed in your browser as a ten-minute walkshed or an A → B path, combining line-of-sight, field-of-view, and per-pass capture probabilities. Each result is reported two ways: as a reproducible research estimate, and as a single Monte-Carlo "live walk." The whole map renders locally in Rust and WebGPU — no location data leaves this page.
